title: Hosted API PRD: scope refinement, eval-gated acceptance, and staged launch playbook
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: This PRD defines the refined scope, acceptance gates, and staged launch checklist for the unified hosted API surface covering chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank. The focus is to lock behavioral contracts and telemetry-driven acceptance criteria so the launch is gated by quality and operational readiness rather than date. This ticket centralizes decisions about scope trims, eval sets, canary slices, and rollback criteria.
scope_inclusions: Unified REST surface for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank with single auth flow
Streaming responses for chat and completions (first-byte streaming + chunked JSON events)
Deterministic response contract for embedding and rerank endpoints (stable response schema)
Per-route telemetry (latency P50/P95/P99, token usage, model fallback rate)
Eval harness integration: predefined eval suites per route (behavioral + semantic tests)
scope_exclusions: Multi-turn session persistence beyond ephemeral KV cache (deferred to Private/Dedicated roadmap)
SAML/SSO account provisioning flows (handled by separate enterprise onboarding ticket)
On-prem installer for Private deployments (out of scope for initial hosted launch)
Built-in reranker model training UI (only inference and score outputs supported)
Custom per-tenant quantization profiles (will be added in Dedicated roadmap)
acceptance_criteria: Behavioral parity: canonical prompts (10 per route) produce >= baseline metric score in eval harness
Quality gates: no more than 2% regression in semantic-similarity on held-out embedding tests vs baseline
Latency SLOs: P95 <= 350ms for short generation routes (<=128 tokens) under canary load profile
Operational readiness: error budget policy configured and automated alerting (paging) wired to on-call
Rollout gating: canary traffic slice (2% of production requests) must meet all eval and telemetry gates for 48 hours
Fallback behavior: when a model variant fallback occurs, client receives explicit header X-RW-Fallback with reason code
Schema stability: embedding and rerank response schemas have published JSON examples and a deprecation policy
Security: KMS integration verified for customer-managed keys in hosted logs redaction test
Docs: Quickstarts for each route exist and complete automated smoke tests (postman/newman) pass
rollout_checklist: Create canary bucket and traffic slicer config (2%, 10%, 50%, 100% steps)
Wire eval harness to CI: nightly run and blocking PR status for canary deploys
Activate route-level telemetry dashboards and set initial alert thresholds
Prepare fallback policies and update SDKs with explicit fallback metadata
On-call runbook updated with de-escalation and rollback playbook
Confluence PRD published and linked in release notes; marketing one-pager drafted
Coordinate with Support to seed triage workspace and canned responses
Archive canary run logs and eval artifacts for postmortem and metrics baseline
tasks: Finalize canonical eval sets for each route (owner: Applied ML)
Lock API contract document and publish JSON examples (owner: API team)
Implement streaming-first-byte behavior for chat endpoints (owner: Serving runtime)
Add X-RW-Fallback header and reason codes across runtime codepaths (owner: Runtime)
Create telemetry dashboard templates and add cost-per-token metric (owner: Observability)
Run cross-team tabletop for rollback scenarios and update runbook (owner: PM)
Validate KMS redaction flows with security and record test artifacts (owner: Security)
Draft SDK changelog and deprecation notes (owner: Developer Experience)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Eval suites may not reflect worst-case customer prompts -> Mitigation: include adversarial set sampled from opt-in beta customers
Risk: Streaming semantics differ across SDKs causing client regressions -> Mitigation: ship a compatibility shim and automated integration tests
Risk: Canary slice too small to surface regional infra issues -> Mitigation: run canary across 3 regions and include synthetic load
Risk: Observability gaps hide slow regressions -> Mitigation: add token-level tracing for 72-hour retention on canary traces
notes: Decision: Use eval-gated launch rather than date-gated. PM to maintain pass/fail criteria and sign-off.
Tradeoff: We deferred tenant-specific quantization to keep hosted launch schedule; this reduces per-token savings but simplifies runtime variants.
Performance note: initial kernel selection will prefer latency-optimized kernels for short sequences; cost tuning happens in Optimize post-launch.
Operational: Dedicated rollback requires both traffic switch and model-state rollback; runbook includes step-by-step commands.
